comments.author: lElwoodBluesl
comments.body_html:
Yes, it’s already pre-configured - in terms of container assignment and spawn rate.

Though spawn rates are definitely something that I will adjust based on user feedback.

In general the mod works as following:

First it parses the database based on parent nodes. The idea behind is that in the handbook each item is listed below a certain category, e.g. graphics card which is below “Barter items - Electronics”. When parsing the database each item is stored in one of the 70 category arrays (e.g. category_Barter_Electronics).

Instead of assigning each of the categories separetely to the 32 container types I created a pre-selection. This pre-selection (e.g. loot_Drawer) is somehow a collection of items you “expect” to find in a certain container type. E.g. a drawer/cabinet gets the pre-selection “loot_Drawers” which contains categories like keys, electronics, tools, info items, etc. Since weapon parts aren’t in e.g. loot_Drawers you won’t find e.g. a magazine or any other weapon part in a drawer/cabinet.

-> You can look up most of the pre-selections’ content in the file config_clearText.txt

-> Info about Shturman’s stash, 5x5 weapon box and 6x3 weapon box are yet not covered in the config_clearText.txt of this release (will probably come in the next release)

The “initial” spawn rate of each item is based on its value/price. The higher the value, the less its initial spawn rate - except the very low value items (0-2000) which have a lower initial spawn rate to avoid having only e.g. ammo rounds in each container

The final spawn rate calculation is:

Initial spawn rate * category rate (* selectedItems_spawnChance)

(selectedItems_spawnChance only is taken into account for items defined by the user)

Those pre-selections finally are assigned to the containers.

To avoid spawning stuff like e.g. developer items (Master hand, Balaclava_dev), Boss items, etc. I added the blacklisting part. If you’re not comfortable with my selection, feel free to remove the according lines in both config.json and config_clearText.txt

Long story short:

If you want to tweak the spawn behavior, the very first thing would be to use the config file, i.e. by adjusting the rate value for each category, e.g. if you want to spawn more info items you would increase the parameter rate_INFOITEMS. If you further want to tweak a specific item then you would need to add the corresponding ID to the config section where it reads “selectedItems_IncreaseSpawnChance”. Within “selectedItems_spawnChance” you would set its spawn rate (keep in mind to put the rate value at the same index position as the ID).

If you want to modify the pre-selections or in general the category assignments to containers you would need to go into the mod.ts itself and adjust the assignments yourself.

Or tell me directly what adjustments you think would make sense.

P.S. if you miss backpacks, they are currently not assigned to any pre-selection/container as most of the backpacks won’t fit in any of the containers (if needed I can add them into the next release).

So from what I saw at Lots of Loot (Default config settings):

comments.author: lElwoodBluesl
comments.body_html:
Hi notAlig. Sure. I will use a simple example with the drawer. btw, meanwhile 1.0.4 uses the default SPT rates but the principle is the same as it was for 1.0.0-1.0.3

“container_Drawer_ItemsDistribution”:[

“1”,“0”

],

“container_Drawer_ItemsDistributionProbabilities”:[

“2761721”,“11522”

],

This block generally adjusts the drawer/filing cabinets spawn rate.

The first section defines the amount of items that possibly can spawn in that container type. In this case either 0 items (=“0”) or 1 item (=“1”). So there will be cabinet slots (throughout the complete map) that either have 0 items or 1 item. Keep in mind, in SPT if an item is too big to fit then it will leave that container empty (can’t change that behavior myself).

The second section defines the actual probability of how often 0 items or 1 item spawn. 2761721 is much bigger than 11522, like such the probability that 1 item spawns is much much higher - though there’s still a slight chance that 0 items will spawn (in one of the cabinets slots).

If you want to increase to a maximum amount of e.g. 2 items, you would do it like such:

“container_Drawer_ItemsDistribution”:[

“1”,“0”,“2”

],

“container_Drawer_ItemsDistributionProbabilities”:[

“2761721”,“11522”,“155555”

],

155555 is just an arbitrary value. You can put the “2” and its spawn rate at any position, like

“container_Drawer_ItemsDistribution”:[

“2”,“1”,“0”

],

“container_Drawer_ItemsDistributionProbabilities”:[

“155555”,“2761721”,“11522”

],

With the behavior mentioned above, i.e. that if an item is too big to fit it could happen that even if you set e.g. 4 items that only e.g. one item spawns in there. The cabinet’s grid size is 2x2. Like such it could spawn 4 times 1x1 items but if it tries to add e.g. an electric drill (2x2) to an existing 1x1 item, it won’t fit - any further spawn is skipped for that cabinet slot and there will be only one item in it.

After checking once more LooseKeyModifier - last time I used it was before 1.0.2, i.e. before it was also adjusting Drawers/Jackets - AllTheLoot WILL have an impact on the behavior of the LooseKeyModifier mod, at least for the static loot in drawers and jackets.

I currently don’t know what’s the average value for “typical” drawer/jacket items in the SPT staticLoot database, i.e. if the “typical” drawer/jacket loot has a rate of 5000 or 50000.

comments.author: lElwoodBluesl
comments.body_html:
With this version you should normally only get errors with not properly set up weapon presets from mods that add custom weapons.

Once there is a faulty part in one weapon preset (a preset basically builds up the complete weapon) you will get the error.

Blacklisting doesn’t work because as long as the preset is available SPT will still try to build up the weapon and if it misses certain parts you’ll get another type of error

What I did instead was “fixing” the issue by actually modifying the preset, i.e. either delete the complete preset (that causes trouble) or by deleting only a specific part of it (e.g. the silencer, magazine).

To find IDs (from parts added by a mod, not the mod itself) the IDs normally can be found in config or database files. Typically the parameter is called “id”, “tpl” and has a somehow random, 24 digit value. For other mods like e.g. the (awesome) mod Gilded Key Storage you will find the necessary IDs in the file config/config.json, though for this mod the item IDs use clear names, like e.g. “Golden_Key_Pouch”.

v1.0.5 doesn’t yet have a global blacklist - but v1.0.6, which will be released with SPT 3.8.0, will have one.

I didn’t put it in the readme. Looking at the code once more, probably would have made sense to add it.

First of all, the initial rates are calculated based on the handbook price. I wanted to avoid the very cheap (specifically weapon part) items of spawning too often, same time I had to guarantee that necessary low value items (like e.g. cheap barter quest items) still have a normal spawn rate. For this I introduced - not accessable via config - the “selectedCategories”, Those categories are:

“BARTER_OTHERS”,
“BARTER_BUILDINGMATERIALS”,
“BARTER_ELECTRONICS”,
“BARTER_ENERGYELEMENTS”,
“BARTER_FLAMMABLEMATERIALS”,
“BARTER_HOUSEHOLDMATERIALS”,
“BARTER_MEDICALSUPPLIES”,
“BARTER_TOOLS”,
“BARTER_VALUABLES”,
“AMMO_ROUNDS”,
“PROVISIONS_DRINKS”,
“PROVISIONS_FOOD”,
“MEDICATION_INJURYTREATMENT”,
“KEYS_MECHANICALKEYS”,
“MONEY”

As soon as the initial spawn rate is assigned, the mod will check for very low value items if the item is part of one of the selected categories or not.

The Tiers are as following:

Tier7“: Item value <2000 and not part of “selectedCategories”

Tier6“: Item value <2000 and part of “selectedCategories”

Tier6“: Item value >=2000 and <20000

Tier5“: Item value >=20000 and <50000

Tier4“: Item value >=50000 and <100000

Tier3“: Item value >=100000 and <400000

Tier2“: Item value >=400000 and <1000000

Tier1“: Item value >=1000000

Hope that helps.

Yes, 1000 or 10 would be the same.

But there are some more steps

Once the initial spawn rate is assigned, one of the next steps is normalization, i.e. all the items in one container are checked to which category they belong, how many items of that category are in the container and how many items are in total in that container. Probability or finally spawn chance is always depending on the min/max relative probabilities, the relative probability for a certain item and the total amount of items in that container type.

Hey man. Great to hear you found a way. Well, the structure behind setting up the loot is not up to me/my mod. AllTheLoot simply adopts to how SPT organizes the loot spawn, i.e. for static loot via container ID, amount of possible items in one container, and chance of how many items will spawn in the container.

comments.author: lElwoodBluesl
comments.body_html:
1. that’s possible but you have to go into the mod source file (AllTheLoot_Main.ts). At the bottom you see the actual assignment of categories. Just search for the category “AMMO_PACKS” and “AMMO_ROUNDS” and add the container of your liking.

For e.g. Ammo rounds go to line 1374 (case SPTLootCategoryName.AMMO_ROUNDS:)

and add below a line according to this way:

this.containerTypeYOURDESIREDCONTAINER.push({…currentItemCopy});

If you want to add it to the green weapon box (the big 5x5 I guess) it’s actually already added, but it’s blocked to spawn because of the item value check.

To counter this, the easiest would be if you go to line 316 and simply add

item.itemLootCategory === SPTLootCategoryName.AMMO_ROUNDS

item.itemLootCategory === SPTLootCategoryName.AMMO_PACKS

Like such - and if you have “AlwaysIncludeWeapons” set to true in the config - rounds and ammo packs will always spawn in 5x5 boxes, even if they are much below the preferred item value.

2. For this you need to go the hard way and find out the corresponding IDs and add them either to the favorite item config or you can add them to the selected items config. Latter allows you to set the spawn chance in a more detailled way (e.g. make ammo type A spawn more likely than ammo type B).

3. If the weapon mod is correctly set up, yes it is possible - and you don’t need to do something specific. In the end AllTheLoot adds everything that’s listed in the handbook, The only thing which could block a weapon to spawn in a container is either the size (if it’s super huge, i.e. above 6x3 size) or if its value is too low/high and it will get removed by the value checker.

comments.author: lElwoodBluesl
comments.body_html:
What do you mean with “new items”? If you mean to add only the items that are currently not in the loot table that would require some tweaks in the code itself.

If you want to keep the vanilla items (incl. their spawn rates) the steps would be to:

- first find out what items you want to add, i.e. which IDs

- then, to avoid doubling the spawn chances if the item is already existing in the loot table and would be added again -> check if those items (IDs) are already covered in the staticLoot.json or not

- rewrite the code in the file “AllTheLoot_FillContainers” at the section where it does the default SPT container overwrite check and instead of providing only the info retrieved in line 40 (i.e. the SPT default loot table), add to this staticLoot variable the “new” items (including hardcoded spawn chances, since filling the containers is the very last action done by the mod and setting spawn chances comes earlier)

- finally, in the “config_Containers_ID.json” set the overwrite flag for all containers to false
